A.explanation: This is about $8.7 \text{ kPa}$ from using $1.4 \text{ m}$ as diameter instead of circumference, giving far too large an area $A = \pi(0.70)^2$.

B.explanation: This is about $35 \text{ kPa}$ from the same too-large area combined with using the whole weight on one area instead of one-quarter of the weight.

C.explanation: Correct per-foot force divided by correct circular area gives about $13500 \text{ N} / 0.156 \text{ m}^2 \approx 86000 \text{ Pa}$.

D.explanation: This is about $340 \text{ kPa}$ from using the total $5400 \text{ kg}$ weight on a single foot area instead of dividing the weight by four.

hints: Notice the $1.4 \text{ m}$ is the circumference $C = 2\pi r$, not the radius or diameter, so first find $r = C/(2\pi)$ for one circular foot.
Connect weight to pressure with $p = F/A$: the force on one foot is one-quarter of $mg$, and the area is $A = \pi r^2$.
Compare $C^2/(4\pi) \approx 0.16 \text{ m}^2$ with $13500 \text{ N}$ per foot to estimate $p$ in $\text{Pa}$, then convert to $\text{kPa}$.
walkthrough: Weight acts through four feet equally, so find the force on one foot. $W = mg \approx 5400 \times 10 = 54000 \text{ N}$, so $F = W/4 \approx 13500 \text{ N}$.
Find the radius from the given circumference. $C = 2\pi r$, so $r = C/(2\pi) = 1.4/(2\pi) \approx 0.223 \text{ m}$.
Find the contact area of one circular foot. $A = \pi r^2 \approx \pi(0.223)^2 \approx 0.156 \text{ m}^2$, which is also $C^2/(4\pi)$.
Calculate pressure as normal force per unit area. $p = F/A \approx 13500/0.156 \approx 86500 \text{ Pa}$.
Convert to kilopascals and round approximately. $86500 \text{ Pa} \approx 87 \text{ kPa}$, closest to $85 \text{ kPa}$. This is option C.
